submission.title: Axial gauge on the periodic lattice: every gauge field reduces to Polyakov loops on one slice
submission.claim: For any group G, any d, L ≥ 1, any direction τ and any link configuration U on the periodic lattice (ℤ/Lℤ)^d, the Lean theorem Contribution.result constructs an explicit gauge transformation g (parallel transport along the τ-line from the slice x_τ = 0) such that: (1) every τ-link off the last slice becomes trivial, (gU)_{x,τ} = 1 whenever x_τ + 1 < L; (2) on the last slice, x_τ = L − 1, the remaining τ-link equals the Polyakov loop P(b) = U_{b,τ} U_{b+τ,τ} ⋯ U_{b+(L−1)τ,τ} of the τ-line through x, with b its point on the slice x_τ = 0; (3) every class-function plaquette action, including the Wilson action of accepted contribution pr-10, is unchanged. This is the axial (temporal) gauge used to build the transfer matrix and Hamiltonian formulation and in Faddeev–Popov arguments on finite lattices. On the torus the τ-links cannot all be removed. The statement pins down the exact obstruction: one Polyakov loop per τ-line. It is the gauge-invariant data that center symmetry acts on.
submission.novelty: This builds on the accepted track result pr-10 (lattice, plaquettes, gauge action, class-function action invariance), which it imports and uses. The mathematics is classical (axial/temporal gauge, e.g. Creutz's and Montvay–Münster's textbooks). In the external Lean library lgt (Douglas), the corresponding step is not proved. lgt's GaugeFixing.lean states that constructing the gauge transform that fixes the axial links 'requires' the tree argument, and its faddeevPopov theorem takes the Faddeev–Popov identity as a hypothesis, hFP. This bundle supplies an explicit, axiom-clean construction for the periodic lattice, any group and any direction, together with the exact Polyakov-loop residue on the last slice.

{
  "version": 2,
  "imports": [
    "Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic",
    "Mathlib.Tactic.Group"
  ],
  "source": "namespace Contribution

open B_fe98bbfbfb97628232bb09c5964d9ee6fa045bd4f96501a460ab0583772ba5a2.Contribution

variable {G : Type} [Group G] {d L : ℕ}

/-- Ordered product `U_{b,τ} U_{b+τ,τ} ⋯ U_{b+(k-1)τ,τ}` of the first `k` links on the
`τ`-line starting at `b`. -/
def linePath (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => linePath U b τ k * U (b + k • e τ) τ

/-- The Polyakov loop: the holonomy once around the periodic `τ`-direction from `b`. -/
def polyakovLoop (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : G :=
  linePath U b τ L

/-- The point of the `τ = 0` slice on the `τ`-line through `x`. -/
def sliceBase (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : Site d L :=
  Function.update x τ 0

/-- The axial-gauge transformation: transport along the `τ`-line from the base slice. -/
def axialGauge (U : LinkConfig G d L) (τ : Fin d) : GaugeTransform G d L :=
  fun x => linePath U (sliceBase x τ) τ (x τ).val

theorem linePath_zero (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) :
    linePath U b τ 0 = 1 := rfl

theorem linePath_succ (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) (k : ℕ) :
    linePath U b τ (k + 1) = linePath U b τ k * U (b + k • e τ) τ := rfl

theorem e_self (τ : Fin d) : (e τ : Site d L) τ = 1 := by
  show (Pi.single τ (1 : ZMod L) : Fin d → ZMod L) τ = 1
  exact Pi.single_eq_same _ _

theorem e_ne {τ μ : Fin d} (h : μ ≠ τ) : (e τ : Site d L) μ = 0 := by
  show (Pi.single τ (1 : ZMod L) : Fin d → ZMod L) μ = 0
  exact Pi.single_eq_of_ne h _

theorem sliceBase_add_e (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) :
    sliceBase (x + e τ) τ = sliceBase x τ := by
  funext μ
  by_cases h : μ = τ
  · subst h; simp [sliceBase]
  · simp only [sliceBase, Function.update_of_ne h, Pi.add_apply, e_ne h, add_zero]

theorem sliceBase_add_val [NeZero L] (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) :
    sliceBase x τ + (x τ).val • e τ = x := by
  funext μ
  by_cases h : μ = τ
  · subst h
    rw [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, e_self]
    simp only [sliceBase, Function.update_self, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one, zero_add,
      ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
  · simp only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, sliceBase, Function.update_of_ne h, e_ne h,
      smul_zero, add_zero]

theorem add_e_apply (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : (x + e τ : Site d L) τ = x τ + 1 := by
  simp only [Pi.add_apply, e_self]

theorem val_add_e_of_lt [NeZero L] (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) (hx : (x τ).val + 1 < L) :
    ((x + e τ : Site d L) τ).val = (x τ).val + 1 := by
  rw [add_e_apply, ZMod.val_add, ZMod.val_one_eq_one_mod, Nat.one_mod_eq_one.mpr (Nat.ne_of_gt (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_add_left 1 _) hx)),
    Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hx]

theorem val_add_e_of_last [NeZero L] (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) (hx : (x τ).val + 1 = L) :
    ((x + e τ : Site d L) τ).val = 0 := by
  have h1 : (x + e τ : Site d L) τ = (((x τ).val + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod L) := by
    rw [add_e_apply]; push_cast; rw [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
  rw [h1, hx, ZMod.natCast_self, ZMod.val_zero]

/-- Away from the last slice, the axial gauge trivializes every `τ`-link. -/
theorem axialGauge_link [NeZero L] (U : LinkConfig G d L) (τ : Fin d) (x : Site d L)
    (hx : (x τ).val + 1 < L) : gaugeAct (axialGauge U τ) U x τ = 1 := by
  simp only [gaugeAct, axialGauge]
  rw [sliceBase_add_e, val_add_e_of_lt x τ hx, linePath_succ, sliceBase_add_val]
  exact mul_inv_cancel _

/-- On the last slice, the remaining `τ`-link is the Polyakov loop through `x`. -/
theorem axialGauge_last [NeZero L] (U : LinkConfig G d L) (τ : Fin d) (x : Site d L)
    (hx : (x τ).val + 1 = L) :
    gaugeAct (axialGauge U τ) U x τ = polyakovLoop U (sliceBase x τ) τ := by
  simp only [gaugeAct, axialGauge]
  rw [sliceBase_add_e, val_add_e_of_last x τ hx, linePath_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
    polyakovLoop, show linePath U (sliceBase x τ) τ L =
      linePath U (sliceBase x τ) τ ((x τ).val + 1) from congrArg _ hx.symm,
    linePath_succ, sliceBase_add_val]

/-- Axial (temporal) gauge on the periodic lattice `(ℤ/Lℤ)^d`, for any gauge group and any
direction `τ`: every configuration is gauge equivalent to one whose `τ`-links are trivial off
the last slice and equal the Polyakov loops on it; every class-function plaquette action
(in particular the Wilson action) is unchanged. -/
theorem result :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (d L : ℕ) [NeZero L] (τ : Fin d) (U : LinkConfig G d L),
      ∃ g : GaugeTransform G d L,
        (∀ x : Site d L, (x τ).val + 1 < L → gaugeAct g U x τ = 1) ∧
        (∀ x : Site d L, (x τ).val + 1 = L →
          gaugeAct g U x τ = polyakovLoop U (sliceBase x τ) τ) ∧
        (∀ f : G → ℝ, IsClassFunction f → latticeAction f (gaugeAct g U) = latticeAction f U) := by
  intro G _ d L _ τ U
  refine ⟨axialGauge U τ, fun x hx => axialGauge_link U τ x hx,
    fun x hx => axialGauge_last U τ x hx, fun f hf => ?_⟩
  exact (B_fe98bbfbfb97628232bb09c5964d9ee6fa045bd4f96501a460ab0583772ba5a2.Contribution.result).1
    G d L f hf (axialGauge U τ) U

end Contribution

{
  "version": 2,
  "imports": [
    "Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic",
    "Mathlib.Tactic.Group"
  ],
  "source": "namespace Contribution

open B_fe98bbfbfb97628232bb09c5964d9ee6fa045bd4f96501a460ab0583772ba5a2.Contribution

variable {G : Type} [Group G] {d L : ℕ}

/-- Ordered product `U_{b,τ} U_{b+τ,τ} ⋯ U_{b+(k-1)τ,τ}` of the first `k` links on the
`τ`-line starting at `b`. -/
def linePath (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : ℕ → G
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => linePath U b τ k * U (b + k • e τ) τ

/-- The Polyakov loop: the holonomy once around the periodic `τ`-direction from `b`. -/
def polyakovLoop (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : G :=
  linePath U b τ L

/-- The point of the `τ = 0` slice on the `τ`-line through `x`. -/
def sliceBase (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : Site d L :=
  Function.update x τ 0

/-- The axial-gauge transformation: transport along the `τ`-line from the base slice. -/
def axialGauge (U : LinkConfig G d L) (τ : Fin d) : GaugeTransform G d L :=
  fun x => linePath U (sliceBase x τ) τ (x τ).val

theorem linePath_zero (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) :
    linePath U b τ 0 = 1 := rfl

theorem linePath_succ (U : LinkConfig G d L) (b : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) (k : ℕ) :
    linePath U b τ (k + 1) = linePath U b τ k * U (b + k • e τ) τ := rfl

theorem e_self (τ : Fin d) : (e τ : Site d L) τ = 1 := by
  show (Pi.single τ (1 : ZMod L) : Fin d → ZMod L) τ = 1
  exact Pi.single_eq_same _ _

theorem e_ne {τ μ : Fin d} (h : μ ≠ τ) : (e τ : Site d L) μ = 0 := by
  show (Pi.single τ (1 : ZMod L) : Fin d → ZMod L) μ = 0
  exact Pi.single_eq_of_ne h _

theorem sliceBase_add_e (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) :
    sliceBase (x + e τ) τ = sliceBase x τ := by
  funext μ
  by_cases h : μ = τ
  · subst h; simp [sliceBase]
  · simp only [sliceBase, Function.update_of_ne h, Pi.add_apply, e_ne h, add_zero]

theorem sliceBase_add_val [NeZero L] (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) :
    sliceBase x τ + (x τ).val • e τ = x := by
  funext μ
  by_cases h : μ = τ
  · subst h
    rw [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, e_self]
    simp only [sliceBase, Function.update_self, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one, zero_add,
      ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
  · simp only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, sliceBase, Function.update_of_ne h, e_ne h,
      smul_zero, add_zero]

theorem add_e_apply (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) : (x + e τ : Site d L) τ = x τ + 1 := by
  simp only [Pi.add_apply, e_self]

theorem val_add_e_of_lt [NeZero L] (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) (hx : (x τ).val + 1 < L) :
    ((x + e τ : Site d L) τ).val = (x τ).val + 1 := by
  rw [add_e_apply, ZMod.val_add, ZMod.val_one_eq_one_mod, Nat.one_mod_eq_one.mpr (Nat.ne_of_gt (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_add_left 1 _) hx)),
    Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hx]

theorem val_add_e_of_last [NeZero L] (x : Site d L) (τ : Fin d) (hx : (x τ).val + 1 = L) :
    ((x + e τ : Site d L) τ).val = 0 := by
  have h1 : (x + e τ : Site d L) τ = (((x τ).val + 1 : ℕ) : ZMod L) := by
    rw [add_e_apply]; push_cast; rw [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val]
  rw [h1, hx, ZMod.natCast_self, ZMod.val_zero]

/-- Away from the last slice, the axial gauge trivializes every `τ`-link. -/
theorem axialGauge_link [NeZero L] (U : LinkConfig G d L) (τ : Fin d) (x : Site d L)
    (hx : (x τ).val + 1 < L) : gaugeAct (axialGauge U τ) U x τ = 1 := by
  simp only [gaugeAct, axialGauge]
  rw [sliceBase_add_e, val_add_e_of_lt x τ hx, linePath_succ, sliceBase_add_val]
  exact mul_inv_cancel _

/-- On the last slice, the remaining `τ`-link is the Polyakov loop through `x`. -/
theorem axialGauge_last [NeZero L] (U : LinkConfig G d L) (τ : Fin d) (x : Site d L)
    (hx : (x τ).val + 1 = L) :
    gaugeAct (axialGauge U τ) U x τ = polyakovLoop U (sliceBase x τ) τ := by
  simp only [gaugeAct, axialGauge]
  rw [sliceBase_add_e, val_add_e_of_last x τ hx, linePath_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
    polyakovLoop, show linePath U (sliceBase x τ) τ L =
      linePath U (sliceBase x τ) τ ((x τ).val + 1) from congrArg _ hx.symm,
    linePath_succ, sliceBase_add_val]

/-- Axial (temporal) gauge on the periodic lattice `(ℤ/Lℤ)^d`, for any gauge group and any
direction `τ`: every configuration is gauge equivalent to one whose `τ`-links are trivial off
the last slice and equal the Polyakov loops on it; every class-function plaquette action
(in particular the Wilson action) is unchanged. -/
theorem result :
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (d L : ℕ) [NeZero L] (τ : Fin d) (U : LinkConfig G d L),
      ∃ g : GaugeTransform G d L,
        (∀ x : Site d L, (x τ).val + 1 < L → gaugeAct g U x τ = 1) ∧
        (∀ x : Site d L, (x τ).val + 1 = L →
          gaugeAct g U x τ = polyakovLoop U (sliceBase x τ) τ) ∧
        (∀ f : G → ℝ, IsClassFunction f → latticeAction f (gaugeAct g U) = latticeAction f U) := by
  intro G _ d L _ τ U
  refine ⟨axialGauge U τ, fun x hx => axialGauge_link U τ x hx,
    fun x hx => axialGauge_last U τ x hx, fun f hf => ?_⟩
  exact (B_fe98bbfbfb97628232bb09c5964d9ee6fa045bd4f96501a460ab0583772ba5a2.Contribution.result).1
    G d L f hf (axialGauge U τ) U

end Contribution

verdict.reason: Accept as a modest formalization of classical finite-lattice axial gauge fixing, not a mathematical discovery or a solution of the Yang–Mills problem. The verified statement constructs a gauge transformation trivializing the selected-direction links away from the final slice and identifies the remaining links with explicitly defined ordered Polyakov products. These definitions express genuine lattice holonomy, and the construction is independently useful marginal work beyond the previously credited gauge-invariance result. Its arbitrary-group and arbitrary-direction formulation provides reusable infrastructure. Action invariance is inherited directly from pr-10 and earns no new credit; that contribution is an acknowledged, verified substantive dependency. The normal-form construction is not merely a repackaging of it. The submission's interpretation needs qualification: a nonabelian Polyakov-loop element is generally gauge covariant by conjugation, rather than gauge invariant; its conjugacy class or class-function evaluations provide invariant data. The submitted theorem does not separately establish the full obstruction criterion, residual-gauge classification, or center-symmetry claims. Credit is limited to the actual construction and residue formula. No measure-theoretic Faddeev–Popov identity, transfer matrix, continuum quantum theory, or positive mass gap is established.

This is concrete, useful reuse, not merely an import or citation. However, the reused mathematics is standard, replaceable infrastructure; the earlier Frobenius identity and vacuum characterization do not contribute to this downstream proof. One modest infrastructure band is justified, without discovery credit.

evidence.claim: On the periodic hypercubic lattice (ℤ/Lℤ)^d, for an arbitrary group G with link variables U : site → direction → G and gauge action U_{x,μ} ↦ g_x U_{x,μ} g_{x+μ}⁻¹, the Lean theorem Contribution.result proves: (1) the plaquette holonomy transforms by conjugation at its base point, so every plaquette action ∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} f(U_p) with a class function f is exactly gauge invariant; (2) for any unitary representation ρ : G → M_n(ℂ) (unitary-valued and multiplicative, predicate IsUnitaryRep), the Wilson action S_ρ(U) = ∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} (n − Re tr ρ(U_p)) is gauge invariant and nonnegative, and S_ρ(U) = 0 iff ρ(U_p) = 1 for every plaquette (all orientations); if ρ is injective, S_ρ(U) = 0 iff U is flat (every plaquette holonomy is 1); (3) for unitary V, 2(n − Re tr V) = ∑_{i,j} |(V − 1)_{ij}|², i.e. the Wilson weight is half the squared Frobenius distance to the identity. Why it matters: these are the exact classical inputs to the lattice route to the mass gap (Wilson 1974; Osterwalder–Seiler strong coupling; Chatterjee's probabilistic program). {
  "version": 2,
  "imports": [
    "Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.UnitaryGroup",
    "Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic",
    "Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic",
    "Mathlib.Tactic.Group",
    "Mathlib.Tactic.NoncommRing"
  ],
  "source": "namespace Contribution

open Matrix

/-! ## Periodic hypercubic lattice, link variables and gauge transformations -/

/-- Sites of the periodic hypercubic lattice `(ℤ/Lℤ)^d`. -/
abbrev Site (d L : ℕ) : Type := Fin d → ZMod L

/-- The lattice unit vector in direction `μ`. -/
def e {d L : ℕ} (μ : Fin d) : Site d L := Pi.single μ 1

/-- A lattice gauge field: one group element on each oriented link `(x, x + e μ)`. -/
abbrev LinkConfig (G : Type) (d L : ℕ) : Type := Site d L → Fin d → G

/-- A lattice gauge transformation: one group element per site. -/
abbrev GaugeTransform (G : Type) (d L : ℕ) : Type := Site d L → G

section General

variable {G : Type} [Group G] {d L : ℕ}

/-- The plaquette holonomy `U_{x,μ} U_{x+μ,ν} U_{x+ν,μ}⁻¹ U_{x,ν}⁻¹`. -/
def plaquette (U : LinkConfig G d L) (x : Site d L) (μ ν : Fin d) : G :=
  U x μ * U (x + e μ) ν * (U (x + e ν) μ)⁻¹ * (U x ν)⁻¹

/-- Gauge action `U_{x,μ} ↦ g_x U_{x,μ} g_{x+μ}⁻¹`. -/
def gaugeAct (g : GaugeTransform G d L) (U : LinkConfig G d L) : LinkConfig G d L :=
  fun x μ => g x * U x μ * (g (x + e μ))⁻¹

/-- Plaquettes transform covariantly: by conjugation at their base point. -/
theorem plaquette_gaugeAct (g : GaugeTransform G d L) (U : LinkConfig G d L)
    (x : Site d L) (μ ν : Fin d) :
    plaquette (gaugeAct g U) x μ ν = g x * plaquette U x μ ν * (g x)⁻¹ := by
  simp only [plaquette, gaugeAct]
  rw [add_right_comm x (e ν) (e μ)]
  group

/-- Reversing the orientation of a plaquette inverts its holonomy. -/
theorem plaquette_swap (U : LinkConfig G d L) (x : Site d L) (μ ν : Fin d) :
    plaquette U x ν μ = (plaquette U x μ ν)⁻¹ := by
  simp only [plaquette]
  group

theorem plaquette_self (U : LinkConfig G d L) (x : Site d L) (μ : Fin d) :
    plaquette U x μ μ = 1 := by
  simp only [plaquette]
  group

/-- A function on the gauge group invariant under conjugation. -/
def IsClassFunction (f : G → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ a b : G, f (a * b * a⁻¹) = f b

/-- The lattice action `∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} f(U_p)` with plaquette weight `f`. -/
def latticeAction [NeZero L] (f : G → ℝ) (U : LinkConfig G d L) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x : Site d L, ∑ μ : Fin d, ∑ ν : Fin d, if μ < ν then f (plaquette U x μ ν) else 0

/-- Any lattice action built from a class function is gauge invariant. -/
theorem latticeAction_gaugeAct [NeZero L] (f : G → ℝ) (hf : IsClassFunction f)
    (g : GaugeTransform G d L) (U : LinkConfig G d L) :
    latticeAction f (gaugeAct g U) = latticeAction f U := by
  have hf' : ∀ a b : G, f (a * b * a⁻¹) = f b := hf
  simp only [latticeAction, plaquette_gaugeAct, hf']

end General

/-! ## The Wilson plaquette weight on `U(n)` -/

section Wilson

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The Wilson plaquette weight `n - Re tr M`. -/
noncomputable def wilsonWeight (n : ℕ) (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (n : ℝ) - (trace M).re

/-- Squared Frobenius distance `‖M - 1‖²` of a matrix to the identity. -/
noncomputable def frobDistSq (n : ℕ) (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n, Complex.normSq ((M - 1) j i)

/-- For unitary `M`, the Wilson weight equals half the squared Frobenius distance to `1`. -/
theorem two_mul_wilsonWeight {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
    (hM : M ∈ unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) : 2 * wilsonWeight n M = frobDistSq n M := by
  have hU : star M * M = 1 := (mem_unitaryGroup_iff').mp hM
  have key : star (M - 1) * (M - 1) = (1 + 1) - star M - M := by
    rw [star_sub, star_one]
    have : (star M - 1) * (M - 1) = star M * M - star M - M + 1 := by noncomm_ring
    rw [this, hU]
    abel
  have hentry : ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ,
      trace (star A * A) = ∑ i : Fin n, ∑ j : Fin n, (Complex.normSq (A j i) : ℂ) := by
    intro A
    simp only [trace, diag, Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.star_apply, Complex.star_def,
      Complex.normSq_eq_conj_mul_self]
  have h := congrArg Complex.re ((hentry (M - 1)).symm.trans (congrArg trace key))
  simp only [Complex.re_sum, Complex.ofReal_re, trace_sub, trace_add, trace_one,
    Fintype.card_fin, Complex.sub_re, Complex.add_re, Complex.natCast_re] at h
  rw [star_eq_conjTranspose, trace_conjTranspose, Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] at h
  rw [frobDistSq, h, wilsonWeight]
  ring

theorem frobDistSq_nonneg (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : 0 ≤ frobDistSq n M :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun _ _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg _

theorem wilsonWeight_nonneg {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
    (hM : M ∈ unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) : 0 ≤ wilsonWeight n M := by
  have h := two_mul_wilsonWeight hM
  have := frobDistSq_nonneg (n := n) M
  linarith

theorem wilsonWeight_eq_zero_iff {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
    (hM : M ∈ unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) : wilsonWeight n M = 0 ↔ M = 1 := by
  constructor
  · intro h0
    have h := two_mul_wilsonWeight hM
    rw [h0, mul_zero, eq_comm, frobDistSq,
      Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun i _ =>
        Finset.sum_nonneg fun j _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg _] at h
    ext j i
    have hi := h i (Finset.mem_univ _)
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun j _ => Complex.normSq_nonneg _] at hi
    have hji := Complex.normSq_eq_zero.mp (hi j (Finset.mem_univ _))
    rw [Matrix.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero] at hji
    exact hji
  · rintro rfl
    simp [wilsonWeight, trace_one]

/-- Conjugation by a unitary matrix preserves the Wilson weight. -/
theorem wilsonWeight_conj {A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hA : A ∈ unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : wilsonWeight n (A * M * star A) = wilsonWeight n M := by
  have ha : star A * A = 1 := (mem_unitaryGroup_iff').mp hA
  simp only [wilsonWeight]
  rw [trace_mul_comm, ← Matrix.mul_assoc, ha, Matrix.one_mul]

/-! ### Wilson action for any gauge group with a unitary representation -/

variable {G : Type} [Group G]

/-- `ρ : G → M_n(ℂ)` is a unitary representation: unitary-valued and multiplicative. -/
def IsUnitaryRep (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ g : G, ρ g ∈ unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ∧ ∀ a b : G, ρ (a * b) = ρ a * ρ b

/-- The Wilson action `S_ρ(U) = ∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} (n - Re tr ρ(U_p))`. -/
noncomputable def wilsonAction {d L : ℕ} [NeZero L] (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (U : LinkConfig G d L) : ℝ :=
  latticeAction (fun g => wilsonWeight n (ρ g)) U

/-- Every plaquette holonomy is the identity. -/
def IsFlat {d L : ℕ} (U : LinkConfig G d L) : Prop := ∀ x μ ν, plaquette U x μ ν = 1

/-- Every plaquette holonomy lies in the kernel of `ρ`. -/
def PlaquettesInKer {d L : ℕ} (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (U : LinkConfig G d L) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ x μ ν, ρ (plaquette U x μ ν) = 1

/-- The representation packaged as a homomorphism into `U(n)`. -/
def IsUnitaryRep.hom {ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ) :
    G →* unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ :=
  MonoidHom.mk' (fun g => ⟨ρ g, hρ.1 g⟩) fun a b => Subtype.ext (hρ.2 a b)

theorem IsUnitaryRep.hom_val {ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ)
    (g : G) : (hρ.hom g).1 = ρ g := rfl

theorem IsUnitaryRep.map_one {ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ) :
    ρ 1 = 1 := by
  rw [← hρ.hom_val, _root_.map_one]; rfl

theorem IsUnitaryRep.map_inv {ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ)
    (g : G) : ρ g⁻¹ = star (ρ g) := by
  rw [← hρ.hom_val, _root_.map_inv]; rfl

theorem wilsonAction_gaugeAct {d L : ℕ} [NeZero L] (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ) (g : GaugeTransform G d L) (U : LinkConfig G d L) :
    wilsonAction ρ (gaugeAct g U) = wilsonAction ρ U := by
  apply latticeAction_gaugeAct
  intro a b
  simp only [hρ.2, hρ.map_inv]
  exact wilsonWeight_conj (hρ.1 a) (ρ b)

theorem wilsonAction_nonneg {d L : ℕ} [NeZero L] (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ) (U : LinkConfig G d L) : 0 ≤ wilsonAction ρ U := by
  unfold wilsonAction latticeAction
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun x _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun μ _ =>
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun ν _ => ?_
  split_ifs
  · exact wilsonWeight_nonneg (hρ.1 _)
  · exact le_rfl

/-- The Wilson action vanishes exactly when every plaquette lies in `ker ρ`. -/
theorem wilsonAction_eq_zero_iff {d L : ℕ} [NeZero L] (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ)
    (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ) (U : LinkConfig G d L) :
    wilsonAction ρ U = 0 ↔ PlaquettesInKer ρ U := by
  have hnn : ∀ x μ ν,
      0 ≤ (if μ < ν then wilsonWeight n (ρ (plaquette U x μ ν)) else 0) := by
    intro x μ ν
    split_ifs
    · exact wilsonWeight_nonneg (hρ.1 _)
    · exact le_rfl
  unfold wilsonAction latticeAction PlaquettesInKer
  rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun x _ =>
    Finset.sum_nonneg fun μ _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun ν _ => hnn x μ ν]
  constructor
  · intro h x μ ν
    have hx := h x (Finset.mem_univ _)
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun μ _ =>
      Finset.sum_nonneg fun ν _ => hnn x μ ν] at hx
    have hlt : ∀ μ ν : Fin d, μ < ν → ρ (plaquette U x μ ν) = 1 := by
      intro μ ν hμν
      have hμ := hx μ (Finset.mem_univ _)
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg fun ν _ => hnn x μ ν] at hμ
      have hν := hμ ν (Finset.mem_univ _)
      simp only [hμν, ↓reduceIte] at hν
      exact (wilsonWeight_eq_zero_iff (hρ.1 _)).mp hν
    rcases lt_trichotomy μ ν with hμν | rfl | hνμ
    · exact hlt μ ν hμν
    · rw [plaquette_self, hρ.map_one]
    · rw [plaquette_swap, hρ.map_inv, hlt ν μ hνμ, star_one]
  · intro h x _
    refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun μ _ => Finset.sum_eq_zero fun ν _ => ?_
    split_ifs
    · exact (wilsonWeight_eq_zero_iff (hρ.1 _)).mpr (h x μ ν)
    · rfl

/-- For a faithful representation the classical vacua are exactly the flat configurations. -/
theorem wilsonAction_eq_zero_iff_flat {d L : ℕ} [NeZero L]
    (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hρ : IsUnitaryRep ρ) (hinj : Function.Injective ρ)
    (U : LinkConfig G d L) :
    wilsonAction ρ U = 0 ↔ IsFlat U := by
  rw [wilsonAction_eq_zero_iff ρ hρ, PlaquettesInKer, IsFlat]
  have key : ∀ p : G, ρ p = 1 ↔ p = 1 := fun p =>
    ⟨fun h => hinj (h.trans hρ.map_one.symm), fun h => h ▸ hρ.map_one⟩
  simp only [key]

end Wilson

/-- Foundations of lattice Yang–Mills on the periodic lattice `(ℤ/Lℤ)^d`:
(1) every class-function plaquette action is gauge invariant, for any gauge group;
(2) for a gauge group `G` with a unitary representation `ρ : G → U(n)`, the Wilson action
`∑_x ∑_{μ<ν} (n - Re tr ρ(U_p))` is gauge invariant and nonnegative, and it vanishes exactly
when every plaquette lies in `ker ρ`; for faithful `ρ`, exactly on flat configurations;
(3) on `U(n)` the Wilson weight equals half the squared Frobenius distance `‖M - 1‖²`. -/
theorem result :
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (d L : ℕ) [NeZero L] (f : G → ℝ), IsClassFunction f →
      ∀ (g : GaugeTransform G d L) (U : LinkConfig G d L),
        latticeAction f (gaugeAct g U) = latticeAction f U) ∧
    (∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (n d L : ℕ) [NeZero L] (ρ : G → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ),
      IsUnitaryRep ρ → ∀ U : LinkConfig G d L,
        (∀ g : GaugeTransform G d L, wilsonAction ρ (gaugeAct g U) = wilsonAction ρ U) ∧
